headline: Showers end tonight; frosty mornings Sunday and Monday, sunny days, uncertain midweek rain, then lower 70s by Friday.
summary: A low pressure system that brought light showers Saturday is sliding southeast, and the showers should taper off this evening. Highs stayed under 60 in most of western Washington. Dry, cooler air is moving in from the northeast, so lows tonight should fall into the mid 30s to mid 40s. Frost is likely early Sunday in the southern Cascade foothills and valleys and south of the Olympics, and a Frost Advisory covers foothills and valleys of Pierce, southern King, Thurston and Lewis counties and the Middle Chehalis River Valley from midnight to 8 AM. Sunday and Monday look mostly clear and dry. Sunday highs should be in the mid 50s to lower 60s, with lows mostly in the 30s. Frost should be more widespread early Monday, including most areas south of Seattle, along Hood Canal and on the north coast, and a larger Frost Advisory runs from midnight Sunday night to 8 AM Monday. Monday should be sunny, with highs in the upper 50s to mid 60s, near normal. Clouds increase Tuesday as a weak atmospheric river (a narrow stream of moisture) aims at British Columbia. Most rain should stay north, but the coast and higher terrain have increasing rain chances Tuesday. The system may drift south late Tuesday into Wednesday and bring rain chances to more of western Washington, though many model runs keep the area dry. High pressure should return Thursday with warmer, drier weather and highs reaching the lower 70s by Friday. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry, sunny stretch and frost through Monday, but less sure about midweek rain and about how long the warmth lasts. A trough (a dip in the jet stream) may bring some rain and cooler weather back by the weekend. Strong northerly winds on the Northern Inland Waters tonight mainly affect small boats.
changes: Earlier discussions called for a chance of rain Tuesday night and Wednesday and warmth from Wednesday night through Friday. The afternoon update starts rain chances on the coast and in the mountains Tuesday, delays the warm-up to Thursday and Friday, stresses that many model runs stay dry midweek, and adds a possible return of rain and cooler weather by the weekend.
